entities.summary: Theodorus of Asine was a Neoplatonist philosopher who lived in the 4th century CE, primarily in Laconia, Greece. Born of unknown parentage, Theodorus was educated in the philosophical traditions of the time, including Neoplatonism and Stoicism. He was a prominent figure in the intellectual circles of Laconia, engaging in debates and discussions with other philosophers and thinkers of the era. Theodorus' philosophical works, though not extensively preserved, are known to have influenced the development of Neoplatonism in the centuries that followed. His legacy is also linked to the rise of Christianity in the region, as his philosophical ideas and teachings overlapped with those of early Christian thinkers. Theodorus' significance extends to his role in shaping the intellectual landscape of Laconia during a period of significant cultural and philosophical transformation. His contributions to the field of philosophy have endured, leaving behind a lasting impact on the development of Neoplatonism and Christian thought.
